name: 2C-T-28
summary: 2C-T-28, also known as 4-(3-fluoropropylthio)-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or as 2C-T-FP, is a psychedelic drug related to 2C-T-7 and 2C-T-21. It was named by Alexander Shulgin but was never made or tested by him, and was instead first synthesised by Daniel Trachsel some years later. It has a binding affinity of 75 nM at 5-HT2A and 28 nM at 5-HT2C.
